title: How should we confirm this problem is fixed?
context: This change is a fix that changes behaviour, so paqad wants proof the problem is gone. A test that fails before the fix and passes after it is the strongest proof; pick another method only when no test can reach the problem.

options.label: Write a test that fails before the fix
options.one_line_preview: If you pick this, a test fails on the old code and passes after the fix, recorded with `paqad-ai fix prove`.
options.trade_off: You give up: nothing for code a test can reach; it needs a runnable test.

findings: EX-qa-engineer-1: the scan must be a function run against planted fixture source as well as the real register.tsx, so each rejected shape (const next, let e, catch (e), next = x, { a: next }, [...e], a non-plain hook parameter, arguments) is proven to fail with its line number and the plugin directory message; a scan of the clean file alone proves nothing

EX-qa-engineer-2: negative cases that must pass: e or next as a parameter of a function passed directly to on(...) or .catch(...), $ as a helper parameter, and arguments only as a property name or inside a string or comment; the scan matches identifiers, not text

EX-qa-engineer-3: the renames to autoTab and event are proven by the existing register tests plus typecheck (unit); the directory acceptance itself is a manual check against the observer tool.check result

EX-qa-engineer-4: given session A has a stage_start with no stage_end in a bundle and session B has written no row there, when B starts, then B's session control is unchanged; and given A has written stage_end, when B starts, then B adopts the bundle (integration, fixture bundles)

EX-qa-engineer-5: boundary cases each need a test: a live stage agent with no open stage_start blocks adoption; a session that already wrote a row in the bundle still adopts it; a passive reader sees no change at all

EX-qa-engineer-6: error path: on a branch whose change is running in another session, the command stops with a non-zero exit, writes no row in that bundle, and the message names the running change and points at --title
EX-qa-engineer-7: moving the rotation to after stage_end must keep a case for /clear between stages still adopting the quiet bundle, so the fixtures are not weakened to pass

EX-qa-engineer-8: a crashed session leaves a stage_start with no stage_end forever, which would block adoption of that bundle for every later session; the spec needs a stated end to that wait and a test for it

EX-qa-engineer-9: given the active change records branch X and Y is checked out, when a bare stage start runs, then the pointer is cleared, the X bundle status is not paused, and a new change opens on Y; boundary cases: detached HEAD and an older bundle with no recorded branch

EX-qa-engineer-10: given delivery.json pr.number 766 and a base branch commit subject ending (#766), the bundle closes at once with status done; negatives that must stay open: (#7660), #766 without parens, pr.number null, and no matching commit within 24h quiet
EX-qa-engineer-11: the 24h quiet wait and git history are flaky-prone: tests inject the clock and build a temp git repo per test with its own cleanup (the known macOS temp-dir race applies)

EX-qa-engineer-12: given the session's HUD snapshot has no qualified change (scope other-branch or none), the line is absent and the agent's stage lines remain; given a qualified change, the line is present (unit)
EX-qa-engineer-13: the same adoption and branch tests run through the Codex hook entry as well as the Claude one, to prove the fix lives in core

options.label: Use a manual check
options.one_line_preview: If you pick this, a person runs a set check to confirm the fix.
options.trade_off: You give up: a fully automated check.

options.label: Keep an approved snapshot
options.one_line_preview: If you pick this, we save an approved snapshot and compare later runs to it.
options.trade_off: You give up: free changes without re-approving the snapshot.

options.label: Use a measured limit
options.one_line_preview: If you pick this, we check a measured value against a set limit.
options.trade_off: You give up: cases the chosen value does not catch.

rationale: Owner: a failing test reproducing each failure first.
